ranges: SPDX and imports: Range/Arc, Bytes, FutureExt/TryFutureExt/BoxFuture and lance_core::Result. Future helpers box ready results and map successful single requests. No runtime initialization occurs in these imports.

array_encoding module is private. Public modules are buffer,compression,compression_config,constants,data,decoder,encoder,encodings,format,repdef,statistics,utils. testing is public only under cfg(test). Public child visibility does not mean every inner implementation is public; exact child APIs remain pending.

Every non-little-endian target triggers compile_error with message Lance encodings only support little-endian systems. The comment describes big-endian support as future work requiring testing, not a supported portable byte-swap path. This is a compile-time gate, independent of optional compressor features.

Public EncodingsIo:Debug+Send+Sync supplies a single-file IO service without requiring lance-io. submit_request borrows self, owns Vec<Range<u64>> and u64 priority, and returns a static boxed future of Result<Vec<Bytes>>. Contract requires one returned Bytes per requested range even after coalescing, and an empty buffer for each empty range. Priority should be the lowest row delivered so late indirect reads can be prioritized. Trait declaration does not enforce range legality, response ordering/count, scheduling, cancellation or durability; implementations/callers own those obligations.

Default submit_single owns one range/priority, calls submit_request immediately, maps Ok through v.pop().unwrap(), then boxes. Upstream Err is preserved. An empty success vector panics while the mapped future is polled; surplus responses silently drop all but the last. No response-count validation or buffer-size check occurs. Correct one-response implementations return their sole Bytes.

Default with_bypass_backpressure returns None. Contract describes a derived IO service for indirect reads to avoid backpressure deadlock/latency; unsupported callers should fall back to self. This default neither clones a service nor changes scheduling.

Default with_io_stats accepts Arc<dyn IoStatsRecorder> but ignores/drops it and returns None. Docs describe additive per-scope accounting without reopening files; unsupported callers fall back to self without scope statistics. No counters, wrapper, global accounting or instrumentation are created here.

Public Debug BufferScheduler privately owns Bytes. new moves that buffer into Self without validating contents, file identity or size. No Clone implementation is declared, although callers can wrap it in Arc.

Private satisfy_request casts both u64 endpoints to usize and calls Bytes::slice on the requested half-open range. It does not validate ordering/bounds, use checked conversions or return Result. On narrower targets casts can truncate; invalid slice bounds reach dependency panic behavior instead of a Lance error. The underlying Bytes slice operation is delegated; the helper contains no explicit payload-copy or allocation loop.

BufferScheduler submit_request consumes ranges in input order, eagerly slices and collects a Vec before constructing future::ready(Ok(...)). Therefore slicing failure occurs at submission, not first future poll. Priority is ignored; empty input returns an empty Vec; valid empty ranges produce empty slices. Returned static future owns collected Bytes, so it does not borrow self. No IO, backpressure, task spawn, cancellation handling, coalescing, stats override or local tests exist; bypass/stats inherit None. Dropping a returned future releases its results, but cannot undo already performed slicing/collection.

Imports older protobuf ArrayEncoding/variant types and aliases, Page BufferType, Nullable arms, shared CompressionConfig, DefinitionInterpretation, Constant and Result. Public empty ProtobufUtils is an associated-function namespace; no stored state, constructor requirement, IO or registration.

ProtobufUtils::constant moves Vec<u8> into protobuf Bytes and wraps Some(ArrayEncoding::Constant). It does not infer data type, require a nonempty value or validate its width. This older array descriptor is distinct from ConstantLayout pages.
basic_all_null_encoding builds Nullable(Some(AllNulls(empty marker))). It has no value/validity children, buffer references or row count; caller supplies those through other metadata.

basic_some_null_encoding owns validity and value descriptors, boxes each under Some and wraps Nullable(Some(SomeNulls(...))). It does not validate the validity bit width, lengths, buffer indices or null population.
basic_no_null_encoding boxes one value descriptor under Nullable(Some(NoNulls(...))). It declares the absence of nulls without inspecting data or adding a bitmap.
block copies any &str into the older Block.scheme string and wraps ArrayEncoding::Block. No recognized-scheme parsing, feature availability or level validation occurs.

flat_encoding stores supplied u64 bits_per_value and a present pb::Buffer with supplied u32 index and Page buffer type. Optional CompressionConfig maps to older string scheme through Display and preserves optional i32 level; None remains absent. There is no positive-bit-width, referenced-buffer or compressor-feature validation. CompressionScheme Display spells fsst,zstd,none,lz4 (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:112-121).

fsl_encoding accepts u64 dimension but converts it with try_into().unwrap() to protobuf uint32, panicking above u32::MAX; zero is accepted locally. It stores has_validity and Some boxed items without checking child count, size or type. This older dimension differs from structural u64 items_per_value. (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:159-165; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:559-565)

bitpacked_encoding stores compressed/uncompressed u64 widths, signed flag and present Page buffer with supplied index. It does not check allowed widths, relative widths or signed representation. No packing is performed.

bitpacked_for_non_neg_encoding stores both u64 widths and a present Page buffer under the distinct BitpackedForNonNeg arm. It does not verify nonnegative input or allowed widths and has no signed argument.
inline_bitpacking stores uncompressed u64 bit width under older InlineBitpacking; the helper emits no width header or payload itself. No validation.

out_of_line_bitpacking stores uncompressed and compressed u64 widths as two direct older-message fields. Unlike structural grammar, compressed values are not represented as a nested CompressiveEncoding here.
variable widens supplied u8 bits_per_offset to u32 and wraps older Variable. All u8 values are accepted; no 32/64-only rule is enforced locally.

fsst boxes the supplied ArrayEncoding as binary and moves Vec symbol table to Bytes. The comment says the mini-block decompressor hard-codes its binary representation and ignores this child, with optimization suggested; that is recorded as comment rationale, not a verified property of every FSST consumer. Constructor still stores the supplied child without validation.
rle stores one u64 bits_per_value in older Rle. It neither computes runs nor checks widths/counts.
byte_stream_split stores one u64 bits_per_value in older ByteStreamSplit. It does not transpose data or ensure width is byte-aligned.

general_mini_block boxes the inner older ArrayEncoding and stores present older Compression with Display scheme string and unchanged optional level. Unlike structural wrapped, this constructor is infallible and does not reject None/Fsst schemes. It does no compression or feature check.

packed_struct moves ordered child descriptors and a present packed Page buffer reference. It does not validate child buffer references, fixed widths, sum of row sizes or compatibility; buffer_index is local metadata, not an absolute file position.
packed_struct_fixed_width_mini_block boxes supplied data under flat and moves ordered Vec<u32> bits_per_values. No check relates those child widths to the child descriptor or a payload row width.

binary boxes independently supplied byte/indices descriptors and stores u64 null_adjustment unchanged. It does not compute offsets, normalize nulls, require monotonicity or validate adjustment against payload length.
dict_encoding boxes indices/items and stores u32 num_items as num_dictionary_items. No key bounds, dictionary uniqueness, null or count validation.
fixed_size_binary boxes data as bytes and stores u32 byte_width, accepting zero locally. It does not check actual payload or child encoding width. This closes the older ProtobufUtils impl.

Private impl_common_protobuf_utils macro accepts module and struct-name identifiers, emits an empty public struct and associated impl. Its sole invocation later substitutes pb21 and ProtobufUtils21. Generated utility methods therefore have concrete public names despite appearing lexically inside a private macro. (rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:670-670)

Generated ProtobufUtils21::flat returns Some(CompressiveEncoding::Flat) with u64 bits_per_value and supplied optional BufferCompression as data. It does not construct a page buffer reference; no width, scheme or level validation. None means no leaf buffer-compression descriptor.

Generated constant wraps Constant with supplied Option<Bytes>; None and Some(empty) remain distinct field-presence states. It builds a compressive descriptor, not ConstantLayout, and does not choose page length/type/nullness or validate literal size.

Generated fsl boxes supplied CompressiveEncoding values and stores u64 items_per_value plus has_validity. No narrowing conversion unlike older fsl_encoding; zero/count/validity consistency remain unchecked.

Generated variable boxes offset descriptor and moves optional BufferCompression for values. It does not encode numeric offsets or establish whether their base is a chunk or payload; physical format implementation owns that.

Generated inline_bitpacking stores uncompressed u64 width and optional BufferCompression for its values. No buffer index or compressed bit width is supplied, and no payload packing or legality check occurs.

Generated out_of_line_bitpacking stores uncompressed u64 width and a boxed nested values descriptor. This differs from older direct compressed-width field; nested descriptor owns the compressed representation. No validation.

Generated buffer_compression returns Result<BufferCompression>, converting runtime CompressionScheme with pb21::CompressionScheme::try_from, casting the enum to i32 and preserving optional level. Conversion accepts Lz4=1 and Zstd=2; None/Fsst return InvalidInput naming the unsupported scheme. No compressor-feature or level-range check occurs in this conversion. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:75-95; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:379-383)

Generated wrapped returns General with Some(buffer_compression(...)) and Some boxed values. Conversion failure propagates via ? before success; no payload transformation is performed. Runtime None is not an accepted way to request an uncompressed General wrapper; omit the optional compression descriptor at the leaf instead where the relevant helper supports it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:82-95)
Generated rle boxes values and run_lengths as separate present CompressiveEncoding children. No run/count validation or packing is done.
Generated byte_stream_split boxes one values descriptor under ByteStreamSplit. This structural tree composition differs from older descriptor containing only bits_per_value.
Generated fsst moves symbol_table Vec to Bytes and boxes nested values. It does not create a general BufferCompression Fsst scheme or validate table/value agreement.

Private generated def_inter_to_repdef_layer exhaustively maps the six DefinitionInterpretation variants to corresponding RepDefLayer i32 codes: AllValidItem1,AllValidList2,NullableItem3,NullableList4,EmptyableList5,NullableAndEmptyableList6. It never emits Unspecified0; no integer cast of the Rust enum is used. (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:54-69; rust/lance-encoding/src/repdef.rs:593-613)

Public generated repdef_layer_to_def_interp first try_from(i32).unwrap(), so an unknown numeric enum value panics. Known Unspecified0 explicitly panics with Unspecified repdef layer. Known values1..6 map to the six interpretations. This helper returns the enum directly, not Result, and supplies no forward-compatibility fallback for new layer codes.

Generated miniblock_layout takes optional rep/def, required value, depth u32, buffers/items u64, optional(dictionary,count), interpretation slice and has_large_chunk bool. It always asserts nonempty interpretations. Some dictionary preserves count including0; None becomes(None,0). Layers preserve input order via mapper, values become Some, and all numeric/large-chunk fields are copied. It does not validate level encodings, repetition depth, counts, buffers or exact-version legality.

Private generated full_zip_layout accepts u8 rep/def widths, selected Details arm, values, interpretations, u32 total and visible items. It widens widths to u32, stores Some details/values, maps layers in input order and returns FullZipLayout. Unlike miniblock_layout it does not assert nonempty interpretations, validate visible<=total, or check widths.

Public fixed_full_zip_layout supplies Details::BitsPerValue(bits_per_value u32) to the private common helper with unchanged widths, values, layers and counts. It does not inspect fixed-width payload or compute bit counts.

Public variable_full_zip_layout supplies Details::BitsPerOffset(bits_per_offset u32) with otherwise unchanged arguments. The oneof distinguishes this descriptor from fixed full-zip even if numeric values match; no offset legality check.

Public generated blob_layout boxes a supplied PageLayout and maps interpretation slice in order; it performs no descriptor/payload IO, null/empty distinction or inner-layout validation. Empty layer slice is accepted locally. This closes impl and macro definition; blank lines have no additional behavior.

Only macro instantiation is impl_common_protobuf_utils!(pb21,ProtobufUtils21). Following inherent impl adds structural-only helpers to that same generated public type. There is no ProtobufUtils23 instantiation or version dispatch here.

constant_layout maps Option<Vec<u8>> to Option<Bytes>, preserving None versus Some(empty), clears rep/def compression and sets both level counts0. It maps layers without asserting nonempty. It does not enforce inline byte limit, scalar type, page buffers or all-nullness; absent inline bytes can accompany an out-of-line scalar elsewhere. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/constant.rs:31-80)

compressed_all_null_constant_layout forces inline_value=None while preserving optional rep/def descriptors and u64 counts, mapping layers in order. Despite its name, it never verifies all-nullness or count/stream agreement; caller owns those invariants. Empty layers and absent streams with nonzero counts are not rejected here.

Structural packed_struct moves ordered Vec<u64> child widths into bits_per_value and boxes required compressed values. This is the fixed-width packed grammar, distinct from older helper taking child ArrayEncoding descriptors and a Page buffer index. No width-sum or type check.

packed_struct_variable moves ordered FieldEncoding vector into VariablePackedStruct. Empty fields and malformed children are not rejected here; exact reader version and codec implementations determine support.
packed_struct_field_fixed creates a FieldEncoding with present supplied value descriptor and BitsPerValue(u64) oneof arm. It neither derives width from data nor validates it.

packed_struct_field_variable creates present value descriptor and BitsPerLength(u64) oneof arm; this is a length-width descriptor, not fixed payload width or an absolute offset. Final braces close function/impl. No local test module, unsafe block, async lifecycle, global state, runtime version branch, byte serialization or codec execution exists in format.rs.
